messages.content: Implement a Python function from a JSON behavioral card. The card is the only task specification. Return a JSON object with a single string field code containing executable Python source. Define solve with the card's exact signature. Use only Python's standard library. Allowed imports: math, itertools, functools, collections, heapq, bisect, statistics, fractions, operator, typing. Do not import or call NumPy, SymPy, NetworkX or any other third-party library. Do not read files, use network, introspection, eval, exec, input or print. Implement computations yourself using built-ins and the allowed standard library. Return plain JSON-compatible values, not iterators or sets; use string keys in dictionaries. Include any helper functions in the code. No tests or main block. Raise ValueError where the card requires it.

Implement this card:
{
  "algorithm": [
    "Perform a depth-first search (DFS) on the graph to identify articulation points",
    "For each node, track the discovery time and low-link values",
    "A node is an articulation point if it has a child in the DFS tree whose low-link value is greater than or equal to the discovery time of the node",
    "Return the list of articulation points in ascending order by vertex index"
  ],
  "constraints": [
    "Vertices are labeled 0 to n-1",
    "Edges are distinct and undirected (given as [u,v] with u < v)",
    "Graph may contain isolated vertices",
    "Articulation points must be returned as strings in ascending order"
  ],
  "edge_cases": [
    "Graph with a single vertex (n=1) has no articulation points",
    "Graph with no edges (n>=2) has all vertices as articulation points",
    "Graph that is biconnected has no articulation points",
    "Graph with multiple connected components: articulation points are identified per component"
  ],
  "inputs": "n: integer >= 1; edges: list of distinct [u,v] pairs where 0<=u<v<n",
  "method_id": "networkx.articulation_points",
  "output": "Ascending list of articulation vertices (as strings) across all connected components",
  "purpose": "Yield the articulation points (cut vertices) of a graph constructed from integer vertices 0 to n-1 and distinct undirected edges",
  "signature": "solve(n, edges)"
}
